newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch find two cases of potato brown rot.
newsitem.headline: Dutch find two cases of potato brown rot.

text.p: Dutch agricultural authorities said on Wednesday they had found two cases of the vicious brown rot potato disease this season but hope to avoid the devastation caused by last year's outbreak.
A spokesman for the Dutch Agriculture Ministry confirmed the finding and said the disease, Pseudomonas solanacearum Smith, had probably infected the plants via the water supply.
The potato-killer is not dangerous to humans but renders the crop unsellable and, once found, forces the farmlands out of use for five years.
An official said testing for the disease had been underway since early August and the fact that only two cases had been found so far indicated the outbreak was not too serious.

The government estimated total damage done by the outbreak which swept across the country last year at 18 million guilders. It paid farmers 8.5 million itself, with the reminder provided by the farmers' umbrella organisation.
Seed potatoes are a key Dutch agricultural export, earning the country some 500 million guilders a year. --Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
